title: HECM Loan Accounting Standard: Monthly Interest and Mortgage Insurance Premium
content:
**Standard.** On a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM), interest and the annual mortgage insurance premium accrue monthly and are posted on the plan's assessment day for the prior month, the month to which both postings belong.

**Balance basis.** The balance basis is the loan balance at the end of the accrual month, that is, every change to the loan balance with an effective date on or before the last day of that month.

**Amounts.** Interest equals the balance basis multiplied by one twelfth of the note rate in effect for that month; the premium equals the balance basis multiplied by one twelfth of the plan's annual mortgage insurance premium rate. Each is rounded half up to the cent, and each posting records the annual rate used. The computation follows the plan's monthly interest method.

**When accrual runs.** Interest and the premium accrue only while the loan status is active, due and payable or deferral period. Nothing accrues for a month that ended before the loan funded, and accrual stops with the month in which the loan is paid in full or claim-terminated; a month whose balance basis is 0.00 posts no entries. Each accrual month is posted once for interest and once for the premium.

**Worked example (hypothetical inputs).** A month-end balance basis of 120000.00, a note rate of 6.000 percent and an annual premium rate of 0.50 percent give interest of 120000.00 multiplied by one twelfth of 6.000 percent, that is 600.00, and a premium of 120000.00 multiplied by one twelfth of 0.50 percent, that is 50.00. A basis of 100001.00 at the same note rate gives 500.005, posted as 500.01.

| Loan status in the month | Interest and premium accrue |
|---|---|
| active, due and payable, deferral period | yes |
| any other status | no |
